items.title: Police hunt parolee missing since Sept 15
items.summary: KULAI: Police are looking for a 30-year-old parolee who has left the Johor Baru parole district without permission since Sept 15. Kulai police chief Assistant Commissioner Tan Seng Lee said police received a report on the man's disappearance on Sept 17. Tan said the man was subsequently listed as wanted.

items.title: 'Disclose your own record': Ex-PJ MP Lee hits back at PKR leader in MBPJ dispute
items.summary: PETALING JAYA: Former Petaling Jaya member of parliament Lee Chean Chung has challenged PKR deputy secretary-general Bryan Ng to disclose his own attendance and voting record at Petaling Jaya City Council (MBPJ) meetings, after being criticised over his participation in council discussions. Lee said an MP was not an MBPJ member but could be invited to attend council meetings as an observer, without voting rights or the authority to approve council papers. He said Ng, an MBPJ councillor, had focused on his attendance at council meetings instead of the policy issues he had raised.

items.title: Today's news in pictures - Friday, Oct 2, 2026
items.summary: NSTP/HAZREEN MOHAMAD [[nid:1546442]] SEPANG – F1 spectators present to watch the free practice session of F1 team drivers for the Formula 1 (F1) Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix (GP) at the Sepang International Circuit (SIC). NSTP/AIZUDDIN SAAD [[nid:1546441]] SEPANG – Spectators attending the Formula 1 (F1) Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix (GP) at the Sepang International Circuit (SIC) wear hats decorated with replica cars. NSTP/OSMAN ADNAN [[nid:1546439]] SEPANG – Fans attend the first free practice session ahead of the Formula 1 (F1) Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix (GP) at the Sepang International Circuit (SIC).

items.title: Selangor Sultan tells political leaders: No fighting, focus on people
items.summary: SHAH ALAM: The Sultan of Selangor, Sultan Sharafuddin Idris Shah, today met and dined with three of the state's Menteri Besar — two former office holders, Dr Mohamad Khir Toyo and Datuk Seri Mohamed Azmin Ali, and incumbent Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari. "This meeting reflects the Sultan of Selangor's continuous concern regarding the state's direction and the people's livelihood, whilst demonstrating the good relationship between the royal institution and the state's administrative leadership, including those who previously shouldered the responsibility," according to a post on the Selangor Royal Office Facebook page. According to the post, Sultan Sharafuddin advised political leaders not to fight, squabble or wrestle for power to the point of triggering division among themselves.

items.title: Anwar provides RM2,000 aid to Tambun crash victims' family
items.summary: IPOH: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today provided RM2,000 in initial assistance to the family of three siblings involved in a road accident in Tambun that claimed the lives of two of them and left another seriously injured. The contribution was handed over by Tambun Parliamentary Community Service Centre officer Muhammad Izzudin Hariz Bohari on behalf of Anwar, who is also the Tambun member of parliament. Tambun Parliamentary Community Service Centre officer Ashraf Kahasani said Anwar had instructed the centre to provide the initial assistance to the family.

items.title: Police seek motivational speaker over alleged child sexual harassment, 'sugar baby' claims
items.summary: KANGAR: Police have asked a freelance speaker to come forward to assist investigations into an alleged child sexual harassment case. Perlis police chief Deputy Commissioner Hamzah Hashim said police confirmed receiving a report concerning the incident involving the speaker at 2.09am on Sept 26. He said the man who is also an independent preacher had been asked to appear at the Padang Besar district police headquarters.

items.title: Saravanan questions why 12-year-old son was brought to MACC HQ
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Former human resources minister Datuk Seri M. Saravanan questioned why the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) did not clarify that his 12-year-old son was not required to attend its headquarters before he brought him there on Monday. In a Facebook post today, Saravanan said they were only informed after entering the premises that his son was not required to sign anything and could return home. Saravanan said he had already informed MACC officers that his son was a minor and had no property in his name.

items.title: Malaysia-China ties must continue to be strengthened, says Zahid
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's long-standing diplomatic ties with China must continue to be strengthened based on the principles of mutual respect and shared benefits, says Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi. The deputy prime minister also expressed hope that close ties between Malaysia and China would continue to grow for the benefit of both countries and their people. "Throughout his tenure in Malaysia, many experiences, achievements and memories have undoubtedly been created together.

items.title: JAC to assemble T9 pickups locally
items.summary: EVOLELECTRIC Motors Sdn Bhd, the Malaysian distributor of JAC pickup trucks, has partnered with FT Assembly Sdn Bhd (FTA), a wholly-owned subsidiary of Feytech Holdings Bhd, to locally assemble JAC's T9 range in the country. The phased completely knocked-down (CKD) programme will cover the T9 petrol plug-in hybrid electric vehicle (PHEV), diesel and battery electric vehicle (BEV) variants. The locally assembled T9 PHEV and BEV are expected to be the first locally assembled PHEV and BEV pickup trucks in Malaysia.

items.title: News@9: Today's top headlines - October 2, 2026 [WATCH]
items.summary: MYEG services suspended The Road Transport Department will suspend MYEG and Zetrix AI as collection agents from Monday over outstanding obligations. Pas open to BN logo Pas president Abdul Hadi Awang says the party is open to using the BN logo in the Melaka election, as talks between the parties continue. Lee quits PKR Petaling Jaya MP Lee Chean Chung will resign from PKR by Monday after the party suspended his membership for three years.

items.title: Rantau Panjang wants its buzz back — and traders hope ECRL is the answer
items.summary: PASIR MAS, Oct 2 — Rantau Panjang was once a bustling border town, alive with the pulse of trade; however, the passage of time and a decline in visitor numbers have left some premises quiet, while the remaining traders continue to hope for a turnaround. The proposal to extend the East Coast Rail Link (ECRL) alignment from Kota Bharu to Rantau Panjang announced by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim is seen not merely as a new transport option, but as a potential catalyst to revitalize economic activities in the town. Rantau Panjang resident Syed Abu Bakar Syed Daud, 65, who has lived in the area for over 50 years said he has personally witnessed the town's transformation, particularly regarding the number of visitors and traders.

items.title: Syed Saddiq: 'Don't splurge for a day and end up in debt for decades'
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: "Do not squander your savings just to splurge for a day and end up saddled with debt for decades," says Muar member of parliament Syed Saddiq Syed Abdul Rahman when asked about the budget for his upcoming wedding to artiste Bella Astillah. Syed Saddiq, 33, said he was taking a serious approach to managing his finances, citing financial issues as a common cause of divorce. Bella said they were collaborating with several brands to provide doorgifts to the first 10,000 guests at both kenduri events.

items.title: Medical assistant drowns while swimming at Chemerong Waterfall
items.summary: Al-Muktafi Billah Shah Fire and Rescue Station operations commander Senior Fire Officer I Kama Suhaimi Abdullah said the victim, Mohd Ikmal Awid, who was stationed at Kemaman Hospital, was found at the scene at noon. Suhaimi said the victim's friend was rescued by their friends, but the victim could not be saved. "About 15 minutes later, his friends made another dive and found the victim at noon," he said.

items.title: Two transporters arrested, 58.1kg ganja seized in Maran
items.summary: Pahang acting police chief Datuk Azry Akmar Ayob said the suspects, aged 44 and 30, were detained around 1.20am while allegedly transferring four bags from the boot of a car in front of a homestay. He said checks on the bags found 56 transparent plastic wrappers and aluminium foil containing dried compressed lumps suspected to be ganja. Azry Akmar said investigations found that the syndicate's modus operandi was to deliver drug supplies to areas where there was demand.

items.title: Treat RM220m international maritime trade issue with same urgency as political cases, maritime expert tells MACC
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 2 — Maritime industry expert Datuk Seri R. Jeyenderan today questioned why an international maritime trade issue involving petroleum cargo worth more than RM220 million had yet to receive a clear answer from the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC), when the commission had moved swiftly on cases involving politicians. “Why is the MACC continuing to remain silent on this issue? Why does it appear that cases involving politicians are being given special attention, while an issue involving international maritime trade has yet to receive a clear answer?”

items.title: RHB Group maintains Malaysia's 2026 growth forecast at 5.4pct
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's gross domestic product (GDP) for 2026 is projected at 5.4 per cent, underpinned by resilient domestic demand and sustained strength in electric and electronic (E&E) exports, according to RHB Group. In RHB's Global Economics Outlook for Q4 2026, group chief economist and head of market research, Barnabas Gan said the bank revised the headline inflation forecast to 1.9 per cent for 2026 from 2.1 per cent previously, reflecting softer-than-expected price pressures. Gan added that domestic policy measures, such as RON95 and diesel subsidy, stable food prices, stable demand conditions and a relatively stable ringgit, as well as gradual pass-through to consumer prices should help keep inflation contained.

items.title: Coach Murad seeks clarity on who was behind threats against Caprice after police drop action against him
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 2 — High-performance transformation coach Syed Mohammad Murad Syed Naseem, better known as Coach Murad or Murad Zaidi, wants to know who was behind an Instagram account that allegedly posted death threats against social media influencer Caprice and his family, after police decided to take no further action against him. “On July 11 last year, Murad Zaidi was arrested in connection with the investigation. “My client has consistently denied being behind the account and cooperated fully with the police investigation,” Aizzat said.

items.title: Foreign man feared buried in Lojing Highlands landslide
items.summary: GUA MUSANG: A foreign man is feared buried in a landslide at workers' quarters on a vegetable farm in the Lojing Highlands here today. Gua Musang Fire and Rescue Station chief Muhammad Azrul Izzham Zulkifli said the department received a distress call at 4.12pm, with a team arriving at the scene, about 92km away, at 5.30pm. Azrul said a search and rescue operation for the man began at 5.54pm, with assistance from the police.

items.title: Existing taxes key to 2027 Budget, expect few major changes: Expert
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia is likely to focus on improving tax collection and fine-tuning existing taxes rather than introducing major new levies in 2027 Budget, according to KPMG senior tax policy adviser Dr Veerinderjeet Singh. He said stronger enforcement, better use of tax agency analytics and broader tax bases could provide additional revenue while supporting the government's fiscal consolidation efforts. Recent measures such as the dividend and capital gains taxes reflect a more progressive tax system, although he does not expect the two per cent dividend tax to be raised or capital gains tax extended to listed shares in the budget.

items.title: 'Marriage isn't just about love' — Siti Hasmah's advice to Syed Saddiq, Bella
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Muar member of parliament Syed Saddiq Syed Abdul Rahman and artiste Bella Astillah said the late Tun Dr Siti Hasmah Mohd Ali was cheerful and in high spirits when they last met her, three days before her death. He said the meeting would remain one of their most cherished memories. Syed Saddiq said Siti Hasmah also offered advice on married life, particularly on the importance of compromise and tolerance between partners.

items.title: PM Anwar hails three more golds as Malaysia matches best-ever Asian Games haul
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 2 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim congratulated Malaysian athletes on winning three more gold medals at the Aichi-Nagoya 2026 Asian Games in Japan today, describing the achievement as a proud accomplishment that reflected their outstanding ability and determination. He said the latest haul brought Malaysia’s gold medal tally to nine as the national contingent continued its campaign to make the Jalur Gemilang proud on the Asian stage, matching Malaysia’s best-ever gold medal haul at the Asian Games, won at the 2010 Guangzhou edition. “Congratulations and well done to today’s gold medallists,” he said in a Facebook post today.

items.title: Anwar congratulates athletes as Malaysia add three more Asian Games golds
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim congratulated Malaysian athletes after the national contingent secured three more gold medals at the 2026 Asian Games in Japan today. He said the feat brought Malaysia's gold medal tally to nine as the national contingent continued its campaign to fly the Jalur Gemilang high on the Asian stage. "Congratulations and well done to all the gold medal winners today," he said in a Facebook post.

items.title: No power struggles, says Selangor Sultan as current and former menteris besar meet
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Oct 2 — The Sultan of Selangor, Sultan Sharafuddin Idris Shah, today met and dined with two former Selangor menteris besar, Mohamad Khir Toyo and Datuk Seri Mohamed Azmin Ali, as well as the current Menteri Besar, Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari. “This meeting reflects the Sultan of Selangor’s continuous concern regarding the state’s direction and the people’s livelihood, whilst demonstrating the good relationship between the royal institution and the state’s administrative leadership, including those who previously shouldered the responsibility,” according to a post on the Selangor Royal Office Facebook page. “His Royal Highness also reminded that Selangor’s progress must be accompanied by societal harmony and administrative stability.

items.title: Malaysia Embraer supply chain: Defence Ministry explores aerospace deal amid RMAF C-390 talks
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia is exploring opportunities to participate in Brazilian aerospace and defence company Embraer's regional and global supply chain as part of efforts to strengthen the local defence industry. Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said this followed a courtesy visit by Embraer Defence and Security chief commercial officer Frederico Lemos at Wisma Pertahanan today. Embraer is a Brazilian aerospace and defence company specialising in aircraft development and integrated defence solutions.

items.title: Farm Price declares maiden dividend since May 2024 listing
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Farm Price Holdings Bhd - a Johor-based wholesaler and distributor of fresh vegetables, food and beverage products and groceries - has declared its first dividend since listing on Bursa Malaysia in May 2024. The company announced a single-tier interim dividend of 0.6 sen per share for the financial year ending Dec 31, 2026, involving a total payout of about RM2.7 million. Managing director Dr Lawrence Tiong Lee Chian said the maiden dividend reflected the group's confidence in its financial performance and cash flow position.

items.title: Amazon to invest US$1bil over five years in US data center communities
items.summary: WASHINGTON: Amazon's cloud computing division said on Friday it would invest more than US$1 billion over the next five years in US communities where it has data centers and vowed to tackle their impacts on electricity and water usage. Data centers, which provide the computing power to train and run AI models, have drawn opposition in communities nationwide over concerns about electricity demand, utility costs and other local impacts. Amazon Web Services said the community investment plans announced on Friday would include spending on education, job training, energy affordability, water and energy preservation and other local priorities in parts of the US where it has data centers.

items.title: iSHAR 2026 focuses on regional Shariah challenges
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Bank Rakyat is strengthening discussions on the future of Islamic finance through the 2026 International Shariah Scholars Roundtable (iSHAR), in collaboration with the Association of Shariah Advisors in Islamic Finance. Bank Rakyat chairman Datuk Mohd Irwan Mohd Mubarak said Shariah research and knowledge development must be grounded in operational realities and evolving economic needs. He said collaboration among financial institutions, regulators, fatwa institutions, academia and industry experts was important to develop relevant and practical Shariah solutions.

items.title: No more bets: 46 nabbed in KL gambling call centre raids
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Police arrested 46 foreigners in raids on nine suspected online gambling call centres across the capital over the past two days. City police chief Datuk Fadil Marsus said the raids were carried out under Op Dadu Khas on Oct 1 and 2. He said 11 of them were remanded for three days from Oct 1 to Oct 3, one was remanded for a day until Oct 2, while another 22 were remanded for four days from Oct 2 to Oct 5.

items.title: Chery adds sporty twist to Tiggo Cross
items.summary: CHERY Malaysia is expanding its Tiggo Cross line-up with the upcoming Tiggo Cross Sport Edition, adding a sportier exterior treatment to its compact SUV range. The model forms part of Chery Malaysia's wider push into sports and e-sports. As part of the partnership, Chery said the Season 18 Legenda prize, coinciding with the 10th anniversary of Mobile Legends: Bang Bang, will be upgraded to a Tiggo Cross Sport Edition.

items.title: Senior citizen held at gunpoint, RM23,000 jewellery stolen
items.summary: Kuala Muda police chief Assistant Commissioner Hanyan Ramlan said the victim was alone at home when the incident occurred around 9.20am. He said the suspect entered the house and pointed the pistol at the victim. Hanyan said the victim suffered bruises on both wrists.

items.title: Berjaya Hills Resort seeks Federal Court leave over RM25.75mil quit rent
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Berjaya Hills Resort Bhd (BHRB) is seeking leave from the Federal Court to appeal against a decision upholding the Pahang government's revision of its quit rent, with the application set to be heard on Dec 8. In a statement today, BHRB said it filed the application on Aug 14 after the Court of Appeal on July 16 upheld the Temerloh High Court's dismissal of its challenge against the revised quit rent rates. The dispute began in 2020 when BHRB said its annual quit rent was increased from about RM2.4 million in 2019 to RM33.7 million, a 13-fold increase.

items.title: Season Optical earns dual recognition from Asean, Asia Records
items.summary: Access to vision care Founded in 2015, Season Optical offers eyewear at different price points, with access to suitable products influenced by factors including cost. Season Optical offers eyewear packages starting from RM28, alongside established brands and higher-priced products. Community vision care Season Optical's activities include corporate social responsibility (CSR) and community programmes involving children and groups that may face difficulties accessing eyewear and vision care.

items.title: Tan Chong, SAIC-GM-Wuling to start EV battery localisation
items.summary: TAN Chong Motor Group and SAIC-GM-Wuling (SGMW) are stepping up efforts to localise electric vehicle (EV) battery production in Malaysia. The companies said localising core EV components would help develop Malaysia's new energy vehicle supply chain and deepen SGMW's industrial presence in Malaysia and the wider Asean region. SGMW's Global 5 Strategy was launched at Caexpo under the theme "Global Wuling, Shining Across Asean".

items.title: Samaiden bags 99.99MW solar contracts
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Samaiden Group Bhd's wholly owned subsidiary Samaiden Sdn Bhd has secured contracts for a 99.99 megawatt alternating current large-scale solar photovoltaic plant. The contracts from Syarikat Pembenaan Yeoh Tiong Lay Sdn Bhd (YTLSB) cover engineering, construction and commissioning works, as well as the supply of solar components. Samaiden said the scope includes the supply and delivery of materials, design, engineering, construction, testing and completion of the solar photovoltaic energy generating facility.

items.title: MARKET PULSE PM OCT 2, 2026 [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Bursa Malaysia closed slightly higher on Friday, with the benchmark FBM KLCI rising 0.03 per cent, or 0.51 point, to 1,630 points after a sell-off. The broader market was positive, with 585 gainers outpacing 541 decliners, while 558 counters were unchanged. Bitcoin was trading at around RM351,675, while Ethereum was trading at around RM11,221.

items.title: Man detained after 230kg of subsidised cooking oil found hidden among rubbish at Melaka restaurant
items.summary: MELAKA, Oct 2 — A Yemeni man in his 50s has been detained today for investigation into suspected unlawful possession of subsidised cooking oil at an Arab food restaurant in Bukit Baru here. Melaka Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry (KPDN) director Dr Mohd Hazimin Jamaludin said 230 kilogrammes of packaged cooking oil worth RM575 were found during an Op Tiris 4.0 raid at the premises at about 1.30pm today. The subsidised cooking oil, comprising various brands, was found in several black plastic bags placed among a pile of dry waste, including old carpets, in a corner of the third floor of the premises, which had been converted into a workers’ dormitory.

items.title: Penang Free School marks 210 years with push for digital transformation
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Oct 2 — Penang Free School (PFS), the oldest English-medium school in South-east Asia, is marking its 210th anniversary this year and is committed to strengthening its digital capabilities to better prepare students for the changing education and technology landscape. PFS Organising Committee chairman Ivan Ooi Jieun Vei said the anniversary celebrations also provided an opportunity to mobilise support for the PFS Digital Transformation Fund, aimed at enhancing the school’s digital infrastructure and capabilities. He said the fund focused on strengthening digital infrastructure, enhancing educators’ capabilities and exposing students to science, technology, engineering and mathematics (STEM), artificial intelligence (AI), robotics, coding and new digital technologies.

items.title: HKL emergency dept upgrade enters final phase, completion targeted by end-2026
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 2 — The upgrading project of the new block of the Emergency and Trauma Department at the Kuala Lumpur Hospital (HKL) is now in the final phase of implementation. The HKL Management said today that several issues require repair and improvement work in the inspection and completion process before the facility can be fully completed. HKL said that it is committed to ensuring that all repair work is carried out properly to meet the facility’s safety, functional, and quality requirements before the project is finalised.

items.title: KL woman fined RM24,000 over fraudulent transfer of retiree’s RM1.1m
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 2 — An unemployed woman was fined RM24,000 by the Sessions Court here today after pleading guilty to two charges of fraudulently transferring RM1.1 million belonging to a retiree into her own bank account eight years ago. Judge Muhammad Ilmami Ahmad imposed the fine on Chin Chew Woon, 43, and ordered her to serve 24 months’ imprisonment if she failed to settle the fine. According to the charges, Chin was accused of transferring RM500,000 and RM600,000 belonging to a 66-year-old man into her bank account in Brickfields on December 26 and 27, 2018.

items.title: JPJ suspends all MYEG Group services from Oct 5 over unresolved contractual obligations
items.summary: In a statement today, JPJ said the suspension covers My E.G. As a result, all JPJ services currently available through MYEG Group channels will be suspended from October 5. Vehicle ownership transfers can meanwhile be carried out through JPJ counters, selected kiosks, the JPJ public portal and eAuto for certain transactions.

items.title: RM5,000 trial payout leads Pontian victim into RM1.15m investment scam
items.summary: PONTIAN, Oct 2 — A private-sector employee lost RM1.15 million after falling victim to an online investment scam operated by a syndicate. Pontian District Police Chief Supt Hadzrat Hussein Mion Hussain said police received a report from the 52-year-old man yesterday, with preliminary investigations finding that the incident began in early January after he got acquainted with a woman via WhatsApp. “Convinced by the investment, the victim subsequently made several more transactions to several bank accounts in stages until March 26, 2026, involving a total of RM1,151,621.96,” he said in a statement today.

items.title: JB-Singapore RTS Link service start pushed back to February 2027
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 2 — Passenger service on the Johor Bahru-Singapore Rapid Transit System (RTS) Link is now expected to begin in February 2027, the Malaysian and Singaporean governments said today. In a joint statement, the Land Transport Authority of Singapore (Singapore Grantor) and the Ministry of Transport Malaysia (Malaysia Grantor) said they had been informed by RTS Operations Pte Ltd (RTSO) of the revised timeline. The new target is subject to RTSO obtaining independent safety certification for the RTS Link and securing final regulatory approvals.

items.title: Johor conservation efforts produce about 5,000 turtle hatchlings a year
items.summary: Johor Department of Fisheries director Rosmawati Ghazali said the main turtle nesting sites identified include Pulau Apil, Pulau Dayang, Pulau Besar and Pulau Tinggi here. However, Rosmawati said turtle eggs left to hatch naturally face a high risk of predation, so they transfer eggs found at nesting sites to hatcheries for closer monitoring. Therefore, we transfer eggs found at nesting sites to hatcheries so our personnel can monitor them more closely,” she said.

items.title: MCMC, MACC to use AI in fight against corruption and abuse of power
items.summary: CYBERJAYA, Oct 2 — The Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) and the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) will leverage artificial intelligence (AI) technology to detect, prevent and manage the risks of abuse of power and misappropriation more systematically and effectively. In a statement today, MCMC said this was among the areas of collaboration agreed upon by the two agencies through the signing of a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to strengthen strategic cooperation in enforcement, corruption prevention and integrity empowerment in addressing complex challenges in the digital environment. The exchange of the MoU between MCMC chairman Tan Sri Mohamad Salim Fateh Din and MACC Chief Commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman took place at the MCMC headquarters here today.

items.title: Department mobilises 153 firefighters, medevac teams and buses to ensure optimum safety during F1
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 2 — A total of 155 officers and members, along with 12 assets from the Malaysian Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM), have been deployed to ensure that the levels of safety, emergency preparedness, and rescue operations are at an optimum level throughout the hosting of the Formula 1 Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix 2026, scheduled to take place at the Sepang International Circuit (SIC). “The assignment of JBPM officers, personnel, and assets to strategic locations is to ensure that any emergency and rescue needs can be addressed quickly, orderly and effectively,” he said in a statement today. He said that 12 departmental assets are being mobilised throughout the event, comprising a Fire Rescue Tender, two Compact Fire Rescue Tenders, one 10,000-litre water tanker, three Emergency Medical Rescue Services ambulances and four JBPM buses.

items.title: Anwar secures fast-track process for missing Malaysians in Nepal
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 2 — Nepalese Prime Minister Balendra Shah has assured Malaysia of full cooperation to determine the status of 54 citizens still missing after devastating floods and landslides in Nepal, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said today. He is willing to give all the cooperation,” Anwar said to reporters this afternoon, adding that Shah agreed during a bilateral call to facilitate administrative and legal efforts to help relatives obtain closure as quickly as possible. The standard legal procedures in Nepal typically require a three-year waiting period to issue a death certificate for missing persons, compared to six or seven years under Malaysian law, Anwar said.

items.title: Police arrest 13 in Teluk Intan raids, syndicate used Alipay accounts to move gambling proceeds
items.summary: TELUK INTAN, Oct 2 — Police have arrested 13 people over a syndicate that allegedly used Alipay accounts opened with Malaysians’ passport details to receive and transfer proceeds from online gambling scams targeting Chinese nationals. Perak police chief Datuk Mohd Alwi Zainal Abidin said the suspects, comprising five Malaysians and eight Myanmar nationals aged between 20 and 44, were arrested in two raids here on Sept 28. Mohd Alwi said the syndicate, believed to have been operating since mid-July, had opened about 60 Alipay accounts using the personal details of local residents.

items.title: Court of Appeal overturns acquittal, jails ex‑bowling coach two more years for molesting 13‑year‑old
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 2 — A former bowling coach, already serving a prison term for sexual assault, was sentenced to an additional two years’ imprisonment by the Court of Appeal today for molesting another former Malaysia Games male athlete in 2017. A three-member bench led by Federal Court judge Datuk Azmi Ariffin, sitting as a Court of Appeal judge, ordered Mat Salleh Jalani to begin serving the two-year sentence after completing his six-year prison term for sexually assaulting a 14-year-old male athlete in 2018. The court reinstated the Magistrates’ Court’s conviction and increased the sentence from 18 months to two years’ imprisonment.

items.title: Thunderstorms expected in KL, Selangor and nine states until 7pm
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 2 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a thunderstorm warning for multiple states across Peninsular Malaysia, Sarawak, and Sabah, forecasting heavy downpours, lightning, and gusty winds until 7pm today. In the weather advisory issued at 4pm, MetMalaysia indicated that the adverse weather will affect the entire northern states of Perlis, Kedah, Penang, and Perak, alongside the Federal Territories of Kuala Lumpur and Putrajaya. In Selangor, seven districts are on alert: Petaling, Sepang, Kuala Selangor, Sabak Bernam, Klang, Kuala Langat, and Gombak.

items.title: Ahmad Maslan urges BN to announce Melaka candidates early, give time to meet voters
items.summary: ALOR GAJAH, Oct 2 — Umno Supreme Council member Datuk Seri Ahmad Maslan has suggested that Barisan Nasional (BN) announce its candidate list for the Melaka state election early. Ahmad, who is also Umno War Room Secretariat chief, said an early announcement would give shortlisted candidates sufficient time to prepare and introduce themselves to voters. Ahmad, who is also Deputy Public Works Minister, said BN’s candidates for the Melaka state election would undergo three levels of screening before a final decision is made by the party’s top leadership.

items.title: KL Marathon goes ahead this weekend, but Kids Dash cancelled over haze concerns
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 2 – The Kuala Lumpur Standard Chartered Marathon (KLSCM) 2026 will proceed this weekend despite the haze, but organisers have cancelled the Kids Dash races to protect the health of young participants. In a race update, organisers said the Full Marathon, ASICS Half Marathon, IHH 10km and 5km will run as scheduled. “We regret to announce that the Kids Dash races will be cancelled, in the best interest of the children,” the organisers said.

items.title: State governments urged to gazette paddy land as rice self‑sufficiency drops to 54.3pc
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 2 — State governments have been urged to gazette paddy-growing areas to sustain rice cultivation and strengthen the country’s food security after the rice self-sufficiency ratio (SSR) declined last year. According to the Agriculture and Food Security Ministry (KPKM), the proposal was among the matters discussed at the second 2026 Agriculture and Food Security Ministers’ Meeting with state agriculture executive councillors, chaired by Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu yesterday. “Malaysia’s reliance on imported rice was estimated at 1.416 million metric tonnes, worth RM2.953 billion, in 2025,” KPKM said in a statement today.

items.title: MCMC probes AI‑manipulated footage of Dr Mahathir grieving wife’s death, warns of legal action
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 2 — The Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) has its eyes on social media content that allegedly uses artificial intelligence (AI) to manipulate footage of Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad grieving the death of his wife, Tun Dr Siti Hasmah Mohamad Ali. The commission said it had contacted the relevant social media platforms over the content. Suspected manipulated content should also be reported to the relevant platforms or authorities.

items.title: Safe return of solo Malaysian after 37 days in Nepal floods offers hope to 54 still missing
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 2 — One of the 55 Malaysians reported to have lost contact following floods and landslides in Nepal last August has been confirmed safe and has returned to Malaysia. Malaysia Solidarity: Families in Hope (MASFIH) spokesman Dr Manivannan Rethinam said the man went to the Malaysian Embassy in Kathmandu on his own yesterday before departing for home and arriving in the country this morning. He said this development means 54 Malaysians remain missing, with all of them travelling in separate groups.

items.title: Anwar: Lee Chean Chung effectively quit PKR for ‘sometime already’
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 2 — Prime Minister and PKR president Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today alleged Lee Chean Chung had been an absentee leader, failing to attend meetings or even the party congress “for over a year”. Lee announced his resignation as Petaling Jaya MP this morning, a move that followed a three year suspension for insubordination. Lee said he would tender his resignation from PKR this Monday.

items.title: Flood mitigation remains Batu pond’s priority as Petra explores supplying 10 million litres daily
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 2 — The Batu flood retention pond could be upgraded into a dual-purpose facility that retains its flood mitigation role while providing up to 10 million litres of alternative water supply daily. The Energy Transition and Water Transformation Ministry (Petra) said the proposed pilot project would provide five million litres per day (MLD) for domestic use, potentially benefiting about 6,000 homes, and another 5 MLD for industrial use in the Batu area. Petra said the project was in line with the National Water Policy’s aim of strengthening water security through more efficient, sustainable and resilient water resource management.

items.title: Tourism Malaysia reports 28.8 million international arrivals Jan–Aug, sector shows steady growth
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 2 — Malaysia’s tourism sector continues to show positive momentum by recording 28.8 million international visitors from January to August this year, a 1.8 per cent increase compared to the same period last year. Tourism Malaysia deputy director-general (promotion) Mohd Akbal Setia said the positive performance reflects the continued appeal of Malaysia as a tourism destination and the importance of strengthening international tourism partnerships. He said this when delivering a speech on behalf of Tourism, Arts and Culture Minister Datuk Seri Tiong King Sing at the opening of the International Tourism, Arts and Culture Exhibition and Conference (INTACT) 2026 at Kuala Lumpur Convention Centre here today.

items.title: Bahrain Crown Prince lands in Malaysia for Sepang F1 Grand Prix weekend
items.summary: SEPANG, Oct 2 — The Crown Prince and Prime Minister of Bahrain, Prince Salman bin Hamad Al Khalifa, arrived in Malaysia today for a special visit in conjunction with the Formula One (F1) Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix at Sepang International Circuit (SIC), which kicks off today. On hand to welcome the Crown Prince were Tunku Temenggong Johor Tunku Idris Iskandar Al-Haj Sultan Ibrahim, Tunku Panglima Johor Tunku Abdul Rahman Al-Haj Sultan Ibrahim, and Tunku Putera Johor Tunku Abu Bakar Al-Haj Sultan Ibrahim. Also present were Youth and Sports Minister Dr Mohammed Taufiq Johari and Bahrain’s Ambassador to Malaysia Dr Waleed Khalifa Al Manea.

items.title: Ministry confirms RM200m arrears owed by Zetrix AI, formerly MyEG, over road tax and licence fees
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 2 — The Ministry of Transport has confirmed that digital services company Zetrix AI Bhd owes the federal government over RM200 million in unremitted public collections. Earlier, the Singapore daily reported, citing official government documents, that Zetrix AI had withheld the collections from the very inception of its three-year service contract in May 2023. An unnamed government official said the ministry was weighing its options.

items.title: Raub police assault: Two Myanmar nationals charged over serious injury to corporal
items.summary: RAUB, Oct 2 — Two Myanmar nationals were brought before the Sessions Court here today to face a joint charge of causing injury to a policeman last month. Judge Siti Hajar Mustaffa then set Oct 14 for case mention to allow a Myanmar interpreter to be present in court. The court also denied bail to both men.
